ops.html: Why this replaces the old plan
ops.src: ## Why this replaces the old plan

ops.html: The current refactor improved AIOS architecture, but it still does not provide RTK/Caveman mechanism parity.
ops.src: The current refactor improved AIOS architecture, but it still does not provide RTK/Caveman mechanism parity.

ops.html: What exists now:
ops.src: What exists now:

ops.html: • Client capability registry is centralized under scripts/lib/clients/.
ops.src: - Client capability registry is centralized under `scripts/lib/clients/`.

ops.html: • Native surfaces are generated from client-sources/native-base/ to Codex, Claude, Gemini, and OpenCode surfaces.
ops.src: - Native surfaces are generated from `client-sources/native-base/` to Codex, Claude, Gemini, and OpenCode surfaces.

ops.html: • Skill sources are canonical under skill-sources/ and synchronized through config/skills-sync-manifest.json.
ops.src: - Skill sources are canonical under `skill-sources/` and synchronized through `config/skills-sync-manifest.json`.

ops.html: • ContextDB can compact historical context with token strategies.
ops.src: - ContextDB can compact historical context with token strategies.

ops.html: • Offload can store large tool output after the tool event and recall it through refs/canvas.
ops.src: - Offload can store large tool output after the tool event and recall it through refs/canvas.

ops.html: • Compression skills describe prompt-level input/output discipline.
ops.src: - Compression skills describe prompt-level input/output discipline.

ops.html: What is missing:
ops.src: What is missing:

ops.html: • No deterministic boundary that intercepts current-turn shell or MCP output before it enters model context.
ops.src: - No deterministic boundary that intercepts current-turn shell or MCP output before it enters model context.

ops.html: • No shared interception engine used by shell, MCP, harness, and client adapters.
ops.src: - No shared interception engine used by shell, MCP, harness, and client adapters.

ops.html: • No compact packet contract that every adapter returns to the agent instead of raw output.
ops.src: - No compact packet contract that every adapter returns to the agent instead of raw output.

ops.html: • No raw-ref store with hash, metadata, recall, redaction, TTL, and metrics as a first-class runtime surface.
ops.src: - No raw-ref store with hash, metadata, recall, redaction, TTL, and metrics as a first-class runtime surface.

ops.html: • No client capability matrix that honestly distinguishes advisory behavior from transparent interception.
ops.src: - No client capability matrix that honestly distinguishes advisory behavior from transparent interception.

ops.html: Therefore the old skill/context/offload-only plan is not enough. It remains useful as a control plane, but RTK/Caveman-style savings require a data plane.
ops.src: Therefore the old skill/context/offload-only plan is not enough. It remains useful as a control plane, but RTK/Caveman-style savings require a data plane.

ops.html: Definition of 1:1 mechanism parity
ops.src: ## Definition of 1:1 mechanism parity

ops.html: 1:1 means replicating the mechanism contract, not copying code or installing competitors.
ops.src: 1:1 means replicating the mechanism contract, not copying code or installing competitors.

ops.html: Required contract:
ops.src: Required contract:

ops.html: • Default interception: when a supported surface is enabled, the agent does not need to remember to save tokens.
ops.src: - Default interception: when a supported surface is enabled, the agent does not need to remember to save tokens.

ops.html: • Pre-context filtering: large shell/MCP/browser outputs are filtered before becoming model-visible context.
ops.src: - Pre-context filtering: large shell/MCP/browser outputs are filtered before becoming model-visible context.

ops.html: • Output brevity: assistant-facing packets and harness reports are compact by default, with precise fallback when safety or ambiguity requires it.
ops.src: - Output brevity: assistant-facing packets and harness reports are compact by default, with precise fallback when safety or ambiguity requires it.

ops.html: • Raw recall: full raw output is still available by ref id, grep, and targeted read.
ops.src: - Raw recall: full raw output is still available by ref id, grep, and targeted read.

ops.html: • Metrics: every shrink/offload decision records raw size, compact size, saved bytes, strategy, fallback reason, and ref id.
ops.src: - Metrics: every shrink/offload decision records raw size, compact size, saved bytes, strategy, fallback reason, and ref id.

ops.html: • Capability honesty: unsupported clients must report advisory/L1, not claim transparent/L3.
ops.src: - Capability honesty: unsupported clients must report advisory/L1, not claim transparent/L3.

ops.html: Non-goals:
ops.src: Non-goals:

ops.html: • Do not install RTK, Caveman, shell hooks, or competitor CLIs.
ops.src: - Do not install RTK, Caveman, shell hooks, or competitor CLIs.

ops.html: • Do not claim raw Codex shell interception if Codex does not expose a pre-tool mutation surface.
ops.src: - Do not claim raw Codex shell interception if Codex does not expose a pre-tool mutation surface.

ops.html: • Do not hide errors, destructive-command risks, secrets, or verification gaps to save tokens.
ops.src: - Do not hide errors, destructive-command risks, secrets, or verification gaps to save tokens.

ops.html: • Host hook/adapter wraps shell calls as an envelope: node scripts/aios-intercept.mjs shell --envelope <base64url-json>.

- Host hook/adapter wraps shell calls as an envelope:

ops.html:
• Shrink tools/list by default:
    • keep name, required params, destructive/safety notes, short description;
    • store full schema/catalog as raw ref;
    • return compact catalog only.

• Shrink tools/call results by classifier:
    • large text/logs: summary + key lines + raw ref;
    • HTML: title/main landmarks/actions + raw ref;
    • large JSON: schema/sample/top keys + raw ref;
    • base64/screenshot: metadata + image/file ref, not inline blob;
    • errors: preserve exact error text and stack head/tail.
This should be the first deterministic cross-client path because it does not depend on each client exposing shell hooks.
